messages:
Anya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I'm seeing short, repeated 429 bursts on r3-l2-quant workloads. Looks correlated with an abrupt KV hit-rate drop and batch collapse. Posting quick traces and a sample log below.

Matt: Which selector change? the heuristic that prefers fast-attn on short sequences?

Anya: Yeah, we biased toward fast-attn earlier in the pipeline. Observed pattern: when fast-attn later fails fallback to slow-attn-compat, batcher keeps trying to form large microbatches, token budget calc halves, and we get waves of soft-429s.

Zane: Can you paste the numbers?

Anya: sure — summary from the 13:02 incident: 
- 3 distinct 429 spikes over ~90s
- avg batch_size before: 8 -> during: 1-2
- KV hit rate: 0.72 -> 0.12
- token_budget target: 256 -> runtime reduced to 120 (due to kernel fallback path)

sample log line:
```
[2026-03-17T13:02:12Z] admit: req_id=abcd kernel_pref=fast-attn kernel_used=slow-attn-compat kv_hit=0.12 queue_len=237 batch_est=1 token_budget=120 soft_reject=prob(0.75)
```

Devon: That matches my local repro from load test. Kernel fallback increases per-token cost and reduces throughput; the batcher keeps waiting for tokens which never arrive because budget was dropped. We need either (A) quicker admission soft-shed when kernel mismatch is detected, or (B) make batcher prefer smaller windows on kernel swap.

Matt: I think we should do both. Short-term: lower the soft_limit threshold so we start probabilistic shedding earlier (e.g., soft_limit = 0.6 * capacity). Medium-term: add a kernel-stability hint to the batcher so it reduces target batch_size for N seconds after a kernel change.

Zane: +1. Also consider making token_budget a moving average with floor (e.g., floor = 0.5 * nominal) so it doesn't collapse so aggressively on transient signals.

Anya: I'll run two canaries: 1) soft_limit=0.6 + prob-shed backoff, 2) kernel_hint: reduce batch_window by 50% for 10s after fallback. Will collect 1h traces.

Matt: Add metric hooks: kernel_swap_count, kv_hit_rate, token_budget_ratio, admitted_batch_size. Dashboards need per-model breakdown.

admit-bot: created ISSUE-1289: "Admission: kernel-fallback -> 429 bursts" assigned to @Anya, priority=P1.

Devon: FYI, check the prefetcher — KV ejection happens ~2s before kernel swap in some runs. If we can prioritize KV retention for the first microbatches after kernel negotiation, hit-rate might recover quicker.

Anya: Good point. I'll instrument KV eviction timestamps and correlate with kernel negotiation. If prefetching interplay is the culprit we might need a short-protected-window where we avoid evicting newly-populated entries.

Matt: Thanks. If canary looks good, roll to staging and set a temporary rollback window. :thumbsup:

Anya: Will post canary results in this thread in ~90m.

Zane: thanks — also leave a note in eng-runtime/room so oncall sees the metrics alert rule tweak.

Anya: noted.
